title: The Four Kingdoms and the Five Works of Sin
description: T77 names the four great kingdoms in the natural mind — four orders of rule articulated as a complete extension of worldly power, none exalted exceedingly above the others. They stand as peers in their own register, each holding its proper place but none claiming the supremacy that belongs only to the Lord's rule above them all. T78 names the four great works of self-love in which the soul, having forgotten that what flows through it is not its own, organizes itself: the appetite of the mouth (consuming for the body's sake), the disorder of the joining (love bent on itself), the love of possession with its boasting, and the lust for dominion with war and tyranny. The soul that hears the teaching and receives the separation of the beautiful from the bad as faith and obedience is lifted above all who remain among the four.
